title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: oOh! Employee
tiers.description: Non-executive Directors, employees, contractors and secondees engaged to provide services to oOh!. Subject to the no-insider-trading rule, the Other Prohibited Actions (short-term trading, margin lending) and the hedging restrictions, and must notify the Company Secretary within 2 business days after trading; no prior approval required unless also Higher risk staff.

tiers.name: Higher risk staff
tiers.description: Officers, staff and consultants privy to oOh!'s market sensitive information: all Directors, ELT members, employees reporting directly to an ELT member, every member of the finance and legal teams, and consultants (including auditors and external legal, tax and accounting professionals) who receive key financial, operational or strategic information. Subject to black-out periods and must get prior written approval before trading.

tiers.name: oOh! Employee (except CEO or CFO)
tiers.description: Higher risk staff sub-group (other than the CEO or CFO); applies to the CEO for approval.

tiers.name: oOh! director (except the Chair of the Board) or CEO or CFO
tiers.description: Higher risk staff sub-group; applies to the Chair of the Board for approval.

tiers.name: oOh! Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Applies to the Chair of the Board Audit, Risk and Compliance committee for approval.

tiers.name: Related Parties
tiers.description: Spouse, de facto partner, child or dependent residing with the oOh! Employee; businesses they or such a person controls (companies, trusts, self-managed and other super funds); or anyone or any business that could influence or be influenced by the oOh! Employee in dealings with oOh!.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions designed to limit the risk of holding securities

windows.end_anchor: the trading day after oOh! announces its full year results
the trading day after oOh! announces its half yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Black-out periods also exist during any period that the oOh! Board specifies from time to time. The Policy does not state whether such periods are disclosed or kept confidential.

rules.section: Glossary (Securities; trade in Securities); Annexure A(2)
rules.detail: Securities expressly include warrants and other derivative products created by oOh! or by third parties (i.e. OTC), and 'trade in Securities' expressly includes entering into hedges or any other transaction in respect of the shares. The approval request must state the proposed trade type (buy, sell, options, hedge, etc.); Higher risk staff must wait for approval and complete the trade within 2 business days.
rules.evidence: warrants and other derivative products and hybrid products in respect of oOh!, whether created by oOh! or by third parties.

rules.detail: Non-Higher-risk employees do not need prior approval to enter a derivative/hedge, but must notify the Company Secretary within 2 business days after trading, and only if not in possession of Inside Information.
rules.evidence: After you or your Related Party trades in oOh! Securities, you must give notice to the oOh! Company Secretary within 2 business days of the trade.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on entering a hedge over unvested rights, particularly unvested equity under any equity plan such as a long-term incentive plan.
rules.evidence: must never enter into any hedge transaction involving: any unvested rights in oOh!, in particular unvested equity under any equity plan operated by oOh! (such as a long-term incentive plan);

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an equity plan.
rules.evidence: any oOh! Securities that have vested, while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any equity plan operated by oOh!;

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked securities is affirmatively permitted, but must not be entered while holding Inside Information; Higher risk staff must first complete pre-trade approval, wait for approval, and hedging during a black-out period is barred except with a hardship/exceptional-circumstances waiver.
rules.evidence: oOh! Employees and their Related Parties are permitted to limit the risk of holding oOh! Securities by hedging, but you and your Related Parties: must not enter into, renew, alter or close out a hedge when in possession of 'Inside Information' or Price Sensitive Information.

rules.detail: Hedging vested, unlocked securities is permitted for non-Higher-risk employees without prior approval, subject to no Inside Information and post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days.
rules.evidence: After you or your Related Party trades in oOh! Securities, you must give notice to the oOh! Company Secretary within 2 business days of the trade.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar hybrid product is a 'derivative product ... in respect of oOh!' and entering into it is 'any other transaction in respect of the shares', so it is a trade requiring prior approval under Annexure A.
rules.evidence: warrants and other derivative products and hybrid products in respect of oOh!, whether created by oOh! or by third parties.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named. They fall within 'derivative products ... in respect of oOh!' under Securities, and if short-dated would be caught by the ban on 'other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts)'; otherwise a CFD is an ordinary trade subject to the applicable approval or notification process.
rules.evidence: trade in oOh!'s Securities on a 'short term trading' basis (buying and selling within a three-month period), and other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts);

rules.detail: Outright ban on trading pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, expressly including using oOh! Securities as collateral for a margin loan or selling them to meet a margin call.
rules.evidence: trade in oOh!'s Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement (including not using oOh! Securities as collateral for a margin loan nor selling them to meet a margin call).

rules.detail: Granting security over shares, including mortgaging them or using them as collateral, is expressly a 'trade in Securities' requiring prior approval; using them as collateral specifically for a margin loan is separately banned outright.
rules.evidence: includes buying, selling, granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral) and entering into hedges or any other transaction in respect of the shares

rules.detail: The same encumbrance-is-a-trade rule applies, but non-Higher-risk employees need only notify the Company Secretary within 2 business days after granting security, rather than obtain prior approval (except margin-loan collateral, which is banned outright for everyone).
rules.evidence: includes buying, selling, granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral) and entering into hedges or any other transaction in respect of the shares

rules.detail: Only margin lending arrangements are expressly banned. Granting security (mortgage/collateral) over vested, unlocked Securities to a lender other than by way of a margin loan is expressly contemplated as a 'trade in Securities', so it is permitted subject to the ordinary prior approval process (confirming no Inside Information, outside a black-out period).
rules.evidence: trade in Securities ... includes ... granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral)

rules.detail: For non-Higher-risk employees, granting security over vested Securities to a lender (other than a margin loan) is a 'trade' requiring only post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, not prior approval.
rules.evidence: trade in Securities ... includes ... granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral)

rules.detail: Ban on 'short term trading' (buying and selling within a three-month period) and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts, subject to the general Annexure B carve-outs (equity plan issue/vesting, passive trades, non-discretionary plans).
rules.evidence: trade in oOh!'s Securities on a 'short term trading' basis (buying and selling within a three-month period), and other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts);

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the trade
clearance.evidence: After you or your Related Party trades in oOh! Securities, you must give notice to the oOh! Company Secretary within 2 business days of the trade.

clearance.post_trade_to: the relevant approver and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days of completing the trade
clearance.evidence: You must wait for approval before trading. Approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of 'Inside Information' prior to trading.

clearance.tier: oOh! director (except the Chair of the Board) or CEO or CFO
clearance.post_trade_to: the relevant approver and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days of completing the trade
clearance.evidence: You must complete your proposed trade within 2 business days of approval from the relevant person. However, if the written approval specifies a different period as permitted for the trade, you may trade during that specified period.

clearance.approver: The Chair of the Board Audit, Risk and Compliance committee
clearance.post_trade_to: the relevant approver and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days of completing the trade
clearance.evidence: If oOh! is in a black-out period approval will not be given except in exceptional circumstances (see 3 below).

carve_outs: issue or vesting of securities under employee, executive or director equity plans operated by oOh!
acquisition of oOh! Securities through a dividend reinvestment plan, share purchase plan or rights issue
disposal of oOh! Securities through acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan
short_term.evidence: trade in oOh!'s Securities on a 'short term trading' basis (buying and selling within a three-month period), and other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts);

exceptions.evidence: issue or vesting of securities under employee, executive or director equity plans operated by oOh! – but the subsequent disposal of any securities is subject to the rules of this Policy;

acquisition of oOh! Securities through a dividend reinvestment plan – however you may only make an election to participate in a dividend reinvestment plan, or a change to your election, outside of a black-out period and at times when you are not in possession of 'Inside Information' or Price Sensitive Information;
the disposal of oOh! Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;

transactions that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the Securities (for example, transfers to the beneficiaries of oOh! Securities already held in a superannuation fund or trust for them) (noting oOh! Directors must still follow normal notification processes);

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, that was not entered into or amended during a black-out period, nor allows any influence or discretion in trading, and that cannot be cancelled during a black-out period, except with the approval obtained under section 3 of Annexure A (for exceptional circumstances);
a disposal of oOh! Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (except that the prohibitions on margin lending arrangements in this Policy still apply);

indirect and incidental trading in units or shares of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold Securities in oOh! as part of its portfolio.

exemption_authority: During a black-out period, Higher risk staff may seek approval to trade only where experiencing severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (Annexure A(3)); the request must confirm no Inside Information and provide sufficient evidence that trading is the most reasonable course of action available, decided by the relevant approver (the CEO, the Chair of the Board, or the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee, depending on the applicant's seniority).

bespoke_clauses.clause: trade in Securities ... includes ... granting options or security over the shares (such as mortgaging them or using them as collateral)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies, oOh! does not ban secured financing generally -- only margin lending arrangements are prohibited outright. Granting security over vested, unlocked shares to a bank (not via a margin loan) is expressly treated as an ordinary 'trade' requiring only the standard approval (Higher risk staff) or notification (other employees) process, making the loan leg of a funded collar structurally available.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale carve-out for secured lenders
bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of oOh! Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights (except that the prohibitions on margin lending arrangements in this Policy still apply)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares under a non-margin-loan secured facility is excluded from the black-out period, short-term dealing, notification and approval requirements, giving the bank a clean enforcement path even during a closed window, provided the facility is not characterised as a margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: oOh! Employees and their Related Parties are permitted to limit the risk of holding oOh! Securities by hedging
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging (and by extension a collar) is affirmatively permitted over vested, unlocked shares, subject only to no Inside Information and the applicable approval/notification process, a materially more permissive starting point than an outright hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trade in oOh!'s Securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement (including not using oOh! Securities as collateral for a margin loan nor selling them to meet a margin call)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the bank's loan were structured or documented as a margin loan, it would be banned outright; the facility should be papered as a bespoke secured loan rather than a margin lending arrangement.

bespoke_clauses.topic: approval automatically withdrawn on inside information
bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval is automatically deemed to be withdrawn if you become aware of 'Inside Information' prior to trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar or loan drawdown lapses automatically if inside information arises before execution, without any separate notice.

bespoke_clauses.topic: black-out period bars hedging absent hardship
bespoke_clauses.clause: If oOh! is in a black-out period approval will not be given except in exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, unwind or roll of the collar by Higher risk staff during a black-out period needs a hardship/exceptional-circumstances waiver, not routine approval.

summary: A funded collar is achievable under oOh!'s policy on vested, unlocked shares, subject to clearance. Hedging is affirmatively permitted (not merely tolerated) once shares have vested and are not subject to a holding lock, provided the individual holds no Inside Information; Higher risk staff (directors, ELT, their direct reports, finance/legal teams and certain consultants) need prior written approval from the CEO, Chair of the Board or Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee Chair (depending on seniority) and cannot trade during a black-out period without a hardship/exceptional-circumstances waiver, while other employees need only notify the Company Secretary within 2 business days after trading. Critically, the secured-financing ban is limited to margin lending arrangements; granting security over vested shares to a bank under a bespoke (non-margin) loan is expressly treated as an ordinary permitted 'trade', and a secured lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the black-out period and approval requirements altogether. Hedging (and any collateral arrangement) is prohibited over unvested rights and over vested shares still subject to a holding lock. Overall, a funded collar over vested, unrestricted shares is workable provided the loan is not structured or documented as a margin loan and the standard pre-clearance/notification and black-out timing rules are observed.
